Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Thursday (October 29) said the Delhi government plans to equip the Food Safety Department with modern equipment and additional staff to strengthen checks against food adulteration.
The announcement follows inspections across the city that detected adulterated and substandard food items.
The department seized 948.9 litres of ghee during inspections at Bhogal Market in south-east Delhi, Najafgarh Market in south-west Delhi and Shiv Vihar in north-east Delhi on Wednesday (October 28), the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) stated. It also collected 15 samples from two of the markets.
Of the seized stock, 389.9 litres came from Bhogal Market and 338 litres from Najafgarh Market. Another 221 litres of suspected adulterated ghee was seized during a joint operation with the Delhi Police in Shiv Vihar, officials said.
The samples have been sent to a laboratory for testing, and further action will be taken based on the results, the CMO stated.
In a post on X, Ms. Gupta stated, “Team Delhi is going all out against adulterated and unsafe food products, not just during the festive season, but throughout the year”.
The Chief Minister said she had issued instructions to blacklist offending brands, impose heavy fines, cancel licences, register FIRs and publicly disclose violators’ names through advertisements. She also directed officials to make consumer helpline numbers available. “Delhiites’ health is non-negotiable,” she wrote.
Ms. Gupta urged people to report cases of adulteration, substandard food and the sale of expired products to the department’s helpline, 1800113921, during office hours.
Ms. Gupta said food safety is directly linked to public health and consumer confidence.
“The government’s responsibility is to ensure that people can purchase food products with confidence that their quality and safety have not been compromised,” she said.
